newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Greek tanker spills oil in western Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Greek tanker spills oil in western Venezuela.

text.p: A Greek tanker ran aground off western Venezuela on Friday night, spilling thousands of barrels of crude into the sea and threatening the shoreline, authorities said on Sunday.

An oil slick about four miles (7 km) long formed in the Gulf of Venezuela, near San Carlos island, following the grounding of the Nisos Amorgos, a spokesman for the state-run oil industry Contingency Plan said.

"We cannot say yet exactly how much oil was spilled ... but it could be one of the bigest oil spills ever in the area," the spokesman, Pedro Marturano, said by telephone from Maracaibo, Venezuela's second city and capital of oil-rich Zulia state.
Unconfirmed press reports said up to 10,000 barrels of oil leaked from the tanker which was carrying 470,000 barrels of crude from Lake Maracaibo to Italy.
Experts using specialized equipment were working to contain the spill and scoop the oil.
Marturano said some of the slick had already reached the sparsely populated Guajira coastline, on the western shore of the Gulf of Venezuela, not far from the small beach resort of Caimare Chico.
He said the tanker chartered by Maraven, a subsidiary of state oil giant Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA), was towed to shore.
